title: Robust and Informative Text Augmentation (RITA) via Constrained Worst-Case Transformations for Low-Resource Named Entity Recognition

problem.claim: Named entity recognition requires token-level classification, while deep learning models often need substantial annotated data and NER annotation is time-consuming and labor-intensive.

gap.claim: Low-resource NER needs methods that can generate useful training data without relying solely on costly manual annotation.

contributions.claim: A textual data augmentation method automatically generates informative synthetic samples for constructing a robust NER classifier.
The method estimates an optimal level of worst-case transformation while preserving the original annotation and uses the transformed data to construct a robust decision boundary.
The paper presents in-depth analyses of generated samples and estimated model parameters.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets in a low-resource setting reportedly show that the method outperforms two baseline augmentation methods, including human annotation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning has improved NER performance, but NER models require substantial annotated data.
The authors propose automatic textual data augmentation that generates informative synthetic samples.
The method estimates annotation-preserving worst-case transformations and incorporates the resulting data into training to construct a robust decision boundary.
Experiments on two benchmark datasets in a low-resource environment reportedly outperform two baseline augmentation methods.
The paper analyzes generated samples and estimated model parameters.

source_observation.claim: Annotation-preserving worst-case transformations are used to generate additional training data and construct a robust decision boundary.

interpretation.claim: Data augmentation can target robustness by generating difficult but label-consistent training examples.

application.claim: For low-resource token-classification tasks, consider augmentation procedures that preserve labels while emphasizing challenging transformations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which transformations are used or when they preserve annotations reliably.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the benchmark datasets.
The abstract does not provide quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not specify the baseline methods or transformation details.
